title: Raven AI lets cops find your home from a photo taken inside
content_md: Photos you take with your phone and some digital cameras can contain hidden information, including where they were taken. You can strip that data out before sharing a photo with someone, which would help to protect your location. But the image itself may still give you away. A company called Graylark says its Raven AI tool can match an indoor photo to a specific property using visual clues alone. No GPS data or view out of the window required. We’ve seen this company before . Its tool, GeoSpy, could work out where a photo was taken by analyzing features in the image, such as vegetation, buildings, and other landmarks. Graylark itself grew out of experiments founder Daniel Heinen and his brothers carried out after reading about using AI to play GeoGuessr , a geography game in which people look at street-level images and try to work out where they were taken. The company has since taken it further. According to 404 Media , Graylark has renamed the tool as Raven and expanded it to identify indoor locations as well. It uses visual clues in the image, without needing location metadata. The tool works by matching images against property photos. An image of something as banal as a washer/dryer sitting in a nook can return a list of ranked results. The tool’s Short-Term Rental ID feature can search what Graylark describes as millions of rental listings worldwide, using an interior photo or a frame from a video.
